YoKPdxWyQT4.title: Islam, Tawheed and Following the Prophet (Reduced Concepts, Episode 2)
YoKPdxWyQT4.one_line: How Islam, tawhid and following the Prophet have been reduced to rituals, a phrase and outward appearance, and what each concept really means.
YoKPdxWyQT4.summary: Continuing the series, he applies the idea of reduced concepts to three core terms. First, Islam: translating deen as religion, a set of rituals to a deity, loses its meaning of what we owe Allah in principles and conduct. The companions' pledges and the questions of the Day of Judgment go far beyond rituals. Islam is a worldview with reform at its heart, refusing oppression, as Surah Hud shows through seven prophets each confronting a different corruption; a domesticated, purely spiritual Islam serves dictators and explains the ruin of the Muslim heartlands. It is practised outside the masjid, which is only a training ground, and the hypocrisy of religious people is a leading reason people leave Islam. Every teaching has a purpose, so parents must give children real reasons. Second, tawhid is not merely a phrase but the single, all-knowing source of ethical red lines, which is why it frees people and why values stay constant, unlike man-made lines that keep shifting. He distinguishes fixed ethics from fiqh, where difference is normal, and mocks those who fight over moon sighting while lying openly. Third, following the Prophet means thinking and treating people as he did, not only dressing like him; the Sunnah is his way, shown in his gentleness with the Bedouin in the masjid. He asks people to keep the outward forms but prioritise the values.

outline.heading: Opening
Values before rulings: the Makkan surahs
outline.gist: Recapping episode one, he notes the Prophet spent thirteen years building principles, and Makkan surahs are value-driven with no legal rulings.

outline.heading: Mushaf order and revelation order
outline.gist: The difference between the order of the book and the order of revelation gives each verse extra dimensions of meaning.

outline.heading: Three concepts for today
outline.gist: He will examine Islam, tawhid and following the Prophet, modelling a method people can apply to other values themselves.

outline.heading: Islam is not 'religion' in the dictionary sense
outline.gist: Dictionary definitions reduce religion to acts of worship for a superhuman being, which is not what deen means.

outline.heading: Language as a source of reduction
outline.gist: Even Arabic speakers now assign different meanings to words than they carried when the Quran and Prophet used them.

outline.heading: Deen: what you owe Allah
outline.gist: Deen shares a root with debt; it is the principles, ethics and behaviours one owes Allah.

outline.heading: The five pillars are not all of Islam
outline.gist: The hadith of Jibril divides the deen into islam, iman and ihsan; limiting it to rituals implies no other obligations exist.

outline.heading: The companions' pledges went beyond rituals
outline.gist: Pledges to give sincere counsel to every Muslim, never to fall but standing, and not to contest leadership without clear cause show the deen's scope.

outline.heading: The questions of the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: We will be asked about our time, wealth, conduct and youth, none of them rituals.

outline.heading: Islam as a worldview and way of life
outline.gist: Islam is the method of serving Allah on earth and touches every detail of life.

outline.heading: Reform is Islam's edge
outline.gist: Remove reform from any ideology and it becomes toothless, which is what those who want the status quo prefer.

outline.heading: Companions content with their own community
outline.gist: Some companions did not want to engage beyond Madinah, but the Prophet taught them Badr was about righteousness, not wealth, and that Islam refuses oppression.

outline.heading: Dictatorships want a quiet Islam
outline.gist: Tyrants are happy for Muslims to practise as long as they never challenge corruption or nepotism.

outline.heading: Surah Hud: seven prophets, seven corruptions
outline.gist: Nuh faced class prejudice, others faced arrogance, entitlement and economic corruption, and Ibrahim faced isolation; each brought a different reform.

outline.heading: A purely spiritual Islam does not work
outline.gist: Reducing Islam to a personal spiritual connection leaves something missing even for someone without heavy trials.

outline.heading: A domesticated Islam and the ruined heartlands
outline.gist: Islam turned timid and quiet, and Palestine, Sham, Iraq, Egypt, Libya and Tunisia, once its centres, are now shells mirroring our hollow values.

outline.heading: Islam is practised outside these walls
outline.gist: People come to the masjid to gain strength to practise Islam outside it.

outline.heading: Hospitals, workplaces, schools and streets
outline.gist: Islam governs our dealings with everyone; the idea that it lives only in the masjid was pushed politically and many have accepted it.

outline.heading: Religious hypocrisy drives people away
outline.gist: A survey of Western Muslims found the conduct of visibly religious people was the top reason for leaving Islam.

outline.heading: What 'praying in the first row' really means
outline.gist: The reward is for arriving early enough to earn the spot, not for blocking in other cars or pushing through rows to get there.

outline.heading: The masjid as a training ground
outline.gist: If the masjid bans all interaction between men and women, it fails to train people to interact respectfully outside, where they must.

outline.heading: Every teaching has a purpose
outline.gist: Allah's laws aim at benefits for the individual and community; teaching purposeless obedience damages the mind.

outline.heading: Growth for its own sake is cancer
outline.gist: As an oncologist he compares purposeless growth to cancer cells; even dawah must have a purpose beyond numbers.

outline.heading: Give children real reasons
outline.gist: Reduced concepts start at home; a meaningless answer either drives a child away or dulls his critical thinking.

outline.heading: Tawhid: the one unforgivable matter
outline.gist: Islam in one word is tawhid, yet it has been reduced to a phrase; why is shirk the one thing Allah will not forgive?

outline.heading: Belief without consequence: the purple planet
outline.gist: If tawhid were only a belief with no effect, like belief in a purple planet, its importance would make no sense.

outline.heading: The red lines concept
outline.gist: Every life has red lines such as murder, theft, lying and adultery; tawhid concerns who draws them.

outline.heading: Who draws the lines?
outline.gist: The West decided lines were drawn by fallible humans, for control, in another time, and so may be redrawn.

outline.heading: How man-made lines shift
outline.gist: Comparing 1920s photographs to today shows how lines are pushed a little each year when their source is not sacred.

outline.heading: Tawhid means one source of ethics
outline.gist: Lines drawn by the all-knowing, all-wise Allah are sacred, so a Muslim dropped into any time or place behaves the same.

outline.heading: A constant source gives constant values
outline.gist: Multiple variable sources yield variable ethics and constant searching for exceptions.

outline.heading: Ethics are not fiqh
outline.gist: Jurisprudential questions like fasting while ill allow differing opinions; ethics and values are a different category.

outline.heading: Fighting over moon sighting while lying openly
outline.gist: People battle over Ramadan calculations and masjid design yet lie to their families; he personally likes moon sighting but it is legitimately disputed.

outline.heading: We cannot differ on honesty
outline.gist: Teaching children to say you are not home teaches them to lie; a believer's values are carved in rock, not drawn in sand.

outline.heading: Tawhid frees people from other masters
outline.gist: Taking direction from a sacred source makes a person a threat to the powerful, who rename vices like alcohol to normalise them.

outline.heading: Shaytan moves the line a millimetre a year
outline.gist: Without a fixed source, values slowly fall until new forbidden things seem normal; tawhid keeps us from lying, stealing, harming and oppressing.

outline.heading: Flexible rulings, fixed lines
outline.gist: Muslims may seek easier fiqh, such as fasting when the sun barely sets, but no one touches the lines Allah drew.

outline.heading: Following the Prophet: the goal is to resemble him
outline.gist: Drawing on his earlier series on intellectual followship, he asks what resembling the Prophet actually means.

outline.heading: Appearance is the easy part
outline.gist: Anyone with money can buy a turban and robe and be treated as holy.

outline.heading: The respirator he wears to keep his beard
outline.gist: He goes through yearly fit-testing for a powered respirator rather than shave, showing he values outward sunnah.

outline.heading: Think the way he thought
outline.gist: He is not belittling appearance; the bulk of following him is processing the world as he did.

outline.heading: Dimensions of his intellect
outline.gist: His planning, broad vision, logic, methodological empathy and civilizational perspective were the subjects of his earlier series.

outline.heading: Sunnah means his way
outline.gist: In the Quran sunnah means a way; emulating anyone starts with their values and conduct, not their socks.

outline.heading: A mystic or a man of wisdom?
outline.gist: Reducing the Sunnah to recommended extras hides the Prophet's intellect and philosophy and makes youth feel they cannot relate to him.

outline.heading: The Sunnah of holding the door
outline.gist: Entering with the right foot means nothing if you push others aside; his way is serving people, as his own teachers did.

outline.heading: The Bedouin who urinated in the masjid
outline.gist: The Prophet let him finish, then gently explained what the masjid is for, and the man learned his deen.

outline.heading: Open hearts that bring people a step closer
outline.gist: His Sunnah is people who love Allah and help others along, even one step at a time.

outline.heading: From one prayer to zero, or to two
outline.gist: A man who prayed only one prayer was berated and stopped praying, until a wiser imam encouraged him to two.

outline.heading: The broken vase and the shisha cafe
outline.gist: A lost young man scolded for breaking something in a masjid found a warm welcome at a shisha cafe and never came back.

outline.heading: Taraweeh reduced to a number
outline.gist: Muslims have argued for centuries over eight or twenty rak'ahs instead of the substance and joy of the recitation.

outline.heading: Take it all, but prioritise the values
outline.gist: Keep the dhikr, the masjid and the outward sunnah, but give the bigger concepts equal attention, as the companions followed him in everything before the details.

outline.heading: Outro

Y1U1ez1QfII.one_line: A sound heart that stays steady, making the hereafter one's concern, and the danger of the world opening up to us.
Y1U1ez1QfII.summary: The first reminder takes Ibrahim's dua in Ash-Shu'ara not to be disgraced on the Day when wealth and children are of no use, only a sound heart. A sound heart is not a spiritual high that rises for a time and then drops again. The Prophet said that whoever makes the hereafter his concern, Allah places richness in his heart, gathers his affairs and the world comes to him humbled, while whoever makes the world his concern has poverty set before his eyes and his affairs scattered, getting only what was written for him. The second reminder recalls the Prophet's words when wealth arrived with Abu Ubaydah: it is not poverty he feared for his followers but the world being spread before them so that they compete for it and are destroyed as earlier nations were. Many who were once guided have been ruined this way, and Allah describes this life as play, adornment, boasting and rivalry in wealth and children. The remedy is perspective: whoever wakes safe at home, healthy, with food for the day, has been given the whole world.

K-BgN8qwbwY.title: The Rituals (Reduced Concepts, Episode 4)
K-BgN8qwbwY.one_line: Prayer, fasting, Hajj, dhikr, dua and khushu as fuel and meaning rather than mechanics, and the danger of giving up on growth.
K-BgN8qwbwY.summary: Calling this the core of the series, he first warns that the real danger is making peace with reduced concepts: a person who keeps striving, however far behind, is better than one far ahead who has stopped, as Imam Ahmad's 'not yet' on his deathbed shows. He then asks whether rituals are a burden or fuel. Salah has been reduced to mechanics that fiqh can validate but that leave youth cold; it is meant as a privileged check-in with the King, a connection, and a way of taking a stand, sustained by love rather than discipline, as the Prophet's joy in prayer shows. Practical steps include pausing one's train of thought and centring the intention before praying. Fasting teaches need versus want, reveals untapped potential, builds compassion, and is not a licence to feast at night; the first Ramadan held Badr. Hajj is not walking around rocks but retracing Adam and Hawwa, Ibrahim's family and the Prophet; Hajar's useless-seeming running teaches us to do our best, and Hajj should be done young. Dhikr must engage mind and heart: alhamdulillah builds optimism and gratitude, subhanallah turns blame inward, and istighfar drives daily improvement and humility. Dua is a conversation, not Aladdin's lamp, and khushu is an emotional response to agreeing with Allah's commands, not tears.

outline.heading: The main course: our rituals
outline.gist: This episode is the heart of the series: the ritual and Islamic concepts the companions received that changed how they lived and thought.

outline.heading: What did these concepts do for them?
outline.gist: We admire the companions' lives but feel unable to emulate them, so we stay in the box we put ourselves in.

outline.heading: The real danger is accepting the reduction
outline.gist: We have made peace with values that no longer function; as long as you have not given up, there is hope.

outline.heading: The striver behind beats the one who stopped
outline.gist: Someone ten steps behind who is still trying is better with Allah than someone far ahead who has stopped holding himself accountable.

outline.heading: The higher you are, the harder the fall
outline.gist: Stopping means falling from a greater height, so the only choice is continued self-awareness and striving.

outline.heading: Imam Ahmad: 'not yet'
outline.gist: On his deathbed he refused Iblis's suggestion that he had made it; Shaytan gives the illusion of arrival to make us stop.

outline.heading: Rituals: fuel or burden?
outline.gist: Most of us experience rituals as an inconvenience in our day, which is the core problem.

outline.heading: Night prayer before a heavy message
outline.gist: The earliest revelations ordered long night prayer because a heavy message was coming; changing words is not enough, we must change how we think.

outline.heading: Salah as the tray that holds every deed
outline.gist: His teacher compared prayer to a serving tray: the bigger your prayer, the more of your other good deeds it can carry.

outline.heading: Mechanics are necessary but not the whole
outline.gist: Without the mechanics prayer is invalid, but a jurist can only rule on the mechanics, not on the connection.

outline.heading: The hundred-metre sprint prayer
outline.gist: In many places prayer has become rapid up-and-down movement with no essence.

outline.heading: Why youth disengage from prayer
outline.gist: A rational mind sees no value in mechanical movements five times a day; prayer is meant to hold us back from sin.

outline.heading: A privilege: checking in with the King
outline.gist: Prayer is the chance to speak to the King of kings five times a day about your fears and hopes; refusing it is beyond rude.

outline.heading: Allah faces the one who prays
outline.gist: Allah turns toward the servant in prayer and asks, when he is distracted, whether he has found something better.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah exists to improve prayer
outline.gist: Nearly every practice of spiritual training aims at making prayer meaningful and bringing peace.

outline.heading: The man told to pray again
outline.gist: The Prophet sent him back three times and then taught him to pray with stillness in each position.

outline.heading: Hit the brakes before you pray
outline.gist: He writes down his train of thought before prayer, then centres himself; that is what intention really is.

outline.heading: Salah means connection
outline.gist: The word means connection, as in the command to pray for the believers; a prayer with no connection is an empty concept.

outline.heading: Establishing prayer means taking a stand
outline.gist: To establish prayer means to take a stand for what you believe and the direction of your life.

outline.heading: Love, not discipline, sustains it
outline.gist: The Prophet's long night prayers and scholars' full recitations came from love; discipline got him through the Quran in one night only once.

outline.heading: Speaking to God five times a day
outline.gist: Explain it to a non-Muslim friend and you sound like the most spiritual person in the room, yet we do not feel it.

outline.heading: The Prophet's joy in prayer and Abu Bakr's tears
outline.gist: Prayer was his rest and the coolness of his eyes; he insisted Abu Bakr, who wept through his recitation, lead the prayer, preserving an example of its depth.

outline.heading: Provoking your own analysis
outline.gist: The aim is for people to examine whether their own values are full or shrivelled and make changes themselves.

outline.heading: Fasting: need versus want
outline.gist: Fasting fills over eight percent of life and teaches the difference between needing and wanting, which the ego blurs.

outline.heading: Clarity when food and desire are removed
outline.gist: Without food and intimacy distracting us, spirituality rises and we get more done.

outline.heading: The inner voice and the first day after Ramadan
outline.gist: A hushed inner voice re-emerges; after Ramadan his workday feels easy and he is more patient than colleagues.

outline.heading: Potential: the question is will you
outline.gist: Ramadan proves you can do more; manage time, hold yourself accountable and raise expectations of yourself.

outline.heading: Eating less and learning compassion
outline.gist: Eating less is healthier, as the Prophet and philosophers taught, and hunger builds empathy for those who suffer.

outline.heading: Not a licence to feast at night
outline.gist: Ramadan is not packing the day's food into one meal or becoming irritable; keep fasting voluntarily afterwards.

outline.heading: The first Ramadan held Badr
outline.gist: In the very first Ramadan the companions fasted in the desert heat and fought the battle that established the Muslim community, the Day of Distinction.

outline.heading: Against the odds, then the last ten nights
outline.gist: Outnumbered three to one with almost no cavalry, they won and returned for the final nights of Ramadan.

outline.heading: Hajj reduced to rocks
outline.gist: Taken literally, Hajj is walking around and between rocks and throwing pebbles; the word means setting out for a destination you value above all hardship.

outline.heading: Pilgrims who did not know why they came
outline.gist: Living in Makkah as a child he saw most pilgrims knew only that Hajj wipes sins, not that rights owed to people remain.

outline.heading: Arafah, Muzdalifah and Mina: Adam and Hawwa
outline.gist: The rites retrace humanity's parents reuniting, forgiving one another and planning how to win back what they lost.

outline.heading: Tawaf: harmony with the universe
outline.gist: Everything from electrons to galaxies circles counterclockwise; tawaf is a prayer, requiring wudu, joining that motion.

outline.heading: Sa'i: rewarded for what you strive toward
outline.gist: Allah rewards what you work toward, not only what you achieve, like someone memorising a line a day who dies with three pages.

outline.heading: Hajar's running: do your best
outline.gist: Her running between the hills changed nothing materially, yet she gave all she had, and Allah brought out Zamzam.

outline.heading: Three layers of the Hajj
outline.gist: Each step echoes Adam and Hawwa, Ibrahim's family, and the Prophet's thoroughly documented Hajj; experience any of them.

outline.heading: The value is the symbolism, not the place
outline.gist: Makkah's landscape has nothing to see; without absorbing the meaning, Hajj becomes rushed mechanics and a status title.

outline.heading: Go to Hajj young
outline.gist: Hajj is physical walking and standing; go after university or early marriage rather than in old age, ideally before children.

outline.heading: Conceptual remembrance
outline.gist: Counted dhikr is essential; his teachers said thousands daily out of sheer joy in saying Allah's name.

outline.heading: Engage the mind and heart, not only the tongue
outline.gist: Begin with the words, then grow into understanding what praise, glorification and tawhid mean.

outline.heading: Alhamdulillah forces optimism
outline.gist: Praising Allah requires finding the good in any situation.

outline.heading: The scholar who lost a leg and a son
outline.gist: On one journey he lost his leg and a son, and praised Allah for leaving him more than He took.

outline.heading: Why Muslims keep rebuilding
outline.gist: The attitude of alhamdulillah is why Muslims, including in Gaza, rebuild and never lose hope.

outline.heading: Gratitude and wellbeing
outline.gist: Psychology shows grateful people live longer and better; focusing on the one missing thing is not living.

outline.heading: Subhanallah turns blame inward
outline.gist: Declaring Allah flawless means asking what I could do about suffering rather than blaming God, and it brings acceptance and sincerity.

outline.heading: Istighfar builds a nation
outline.gist: Sincerely acknowledging a mistake each day means improving each day, which is why the Quran ties seeking forgiveness to rain and flourishing.

outline.heading: Istighfar and humility
outline.gist: Focusing on your own sins leaves no room to feel superior to others.

outline.heading: Dua is not Aladdin's lamp
outline.gist: Dua is an ongoing conversation; Allah answers by granting now, later, something better, or averting harm.

outline.heading: Ramadan is designed for dua
outline.gist: Use Ramadan to build the habit of taking your hopes and fears to Allah all year.

outline.heading: Khushu: an emotional response to agreement
outline.gist: His definition: an emotional response to mentally agreeing with and accepting Allah's commands, like going to the pharmacy at night grudgingly or gladly.

outline.heading: Try it in prayer; it is not tears
outline.gist: Stand in prayer grateful to be exactly where you should be; reducing khushu to crying misses the point, and not everyone can cry.

outline.heading: Outro

39:71.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا فُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ رُسُلࣱ مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُونَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكُمۡ وَيُنذِرُونَكُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَاۚ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنۡ حَقَّتۡ كَلِمَةُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
39:71.en: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates are opened and its keepers will say, "Did there not come to you messengers from yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers

39:72.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلُوٓاْ أَبۡوَٰبَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ مَثۡوَى ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
39:72.en: [To them] it will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant

39:73.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ رَبَّهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ طِبۡتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُوهَا خَٰلِدِينَ
39:73.en: But those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, "Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein," [they will enter]

40:28.ar: وَقَالَ رَجُلࣱ مُّؤۡمِنࣱ مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَكۡتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥٓ أَتَقۡتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ ٱللَّهُ وَقَدۡ جَآءَكُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ مِن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ وَإِن يَكُ كَٰذِبࣰ ا فَعَلَيۡهِ كَذِبُهُۥۖ وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقࣰ ا يُصِبۡكُم بَعۡضُ ٱلَّذِي يَعِدُكُمۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ مُسۡرِفࣱ كَذَّابࣱ‏
40:28.en: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, "Do you kill a man [merely] because he says, 'My Lord is Allah' while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he should be lying, then upon him is [the consequence of] his lie; but if he should be truthful, there will strike you some of what he promises you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar

40:56.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَٰدِلُونَ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ سُلۡطَٰنٍ أَتَىٰهُمۡ إِن فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ إِلَّا كِبۡرࣱ مَّا هُم بِبَٰلِغِيهِۚ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
40:56.en: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without [any] authority having come to them - there is not within their breasts except pride, [the extent of] which they cannot reach. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing

41:34.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةࣱ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمࣱ‏
41:34.en: And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend

41:35.ar: وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
41:35.en: But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one having a great portion [of good]

42:15.ar: فَلِذَٰلِكَ فَٱدۡعُۖ وَٱسۡتَقِمۡ كَمَآ أُمِرۡتَۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۖ وَقُلۡ ءَامَنتُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن كِتَٰبࣲۖ وَأُمِرۡتُ لِأَعۡدِلَ بَيۡنَكُمُۖ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمۡۖ لَنَآ أَعۡمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡۖ لَا حُجَّةَ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمُۖ ٱللَّهُ يَجۡمَعُ بَيۡنَنَاۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
42:15.en: So to that [religion of Allah] invite, [O Muhammad], and remain on a right course as you are commanded and do not follow their inclinations but say, "I have believed in what Allah has revealed of the Qur'an, and I have been commanded to do justice among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you your deeds. There is no [need for] argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the [final] destination

42:38.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمۡ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَمۡرُهُمۡ شُورَىٰ بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
42:38.en: And those who have responded to their lord and established prayer and whose affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves, and from what We have provided them, they spend

3:159.ar: فَبِمَا رَحۡمَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلۡقَلۡبِ لَٱنفَضُّواْ مِنۡ حَوۡلِكَۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمۡتَ فَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
3:159.en: So by mercy from Allah, [O Muhammad], you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely [upon Him]

nCZBT5koNlQ.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 23: Quranic Reflections (Az-Zumar 62 to Ash-Shura 23)
nCZBT5koNlQ.one_line: The Ha-Mim surahs as a manual for dawah: connection with Allah, example, reference and consultation, plus free belief, advocacy, repelling evil with good and arrogance.
nCZBT5koNlQ.summary: He introduces the Ha-Mim surahs as a cluster on carrying Islam to other people, each giving advice on what to do and what to avoid. Ghafir pairs taking the message to those who argue with constant dua, since you cannot call people to a God you do not know; Fussilat shows that dawah through conduct works better than words; Ash-Shura requires a reference and a community run by consultation. He presses that Muslim communities and institutions in the West rarely consult their people or one another, citing the Prophet's habit of withholding his view and following the majority before Uhud. From the end of az-Zumar he teaches that no one walks to Paradise alone, so choose your group, and contrasts the closed and open gates of Hell and Paradise. The believer from Pharaoh's family leads him to freedom of belief, the persecution of speech through cancellation, the narrowing range of acceptable opinion since October 7, the difference between Zionism and Judaism, and the need for communities to organise and back those who speak instead of demanding courage from imams alone. He closes with repelling evil with excellence, a verse balancing conviction with tolerance, and arrogance as the root of rejecting truth.

outline.heading: Opening
The Ha-Mim cluster: carrying dawah to individuals
outline.gist: From Ghafir to al-Ahqaf the surahs share an opening, the story of Musa and paired positive and negative advice on carrying Islam to other individuals, unlike the earlier cluster about carrying the message as a nation-building way of life.

outline.heading: Ghafir: take dawah to those who argue, while making dua
outline.gist: Bring the message to those who oppose it and, in parallel, keep a personal connection with Allah; calling people to a God you do not know is counterproductive.

outline.heading: Fussilat: dawah through behaviour works better
outline.gist: Those who keep refusing spoken dawah are held to account, while dawah through conduct forces no one to listen and has more impact.

outline.heading: Ash-Shura: dawah needs a reference
outline.gist: Without a body of knowledge to refer people to you either look lost or make up answers that cause harm.

outline.heading: Shura as consultation: your voice matters
outline.gist: Consultation is the closest Islamic idea to democracy: even if you are not the leader you have a say in decisions that affect the group, as the Prophet taught and the surah describes.

outline.heading: Without consultation the dawah goes nowhere
outline.gist: These three surahs give positive advice and the next three warn of pitfalls; if everyone works alone in silos with no consultation, the message will not be carried far.

outline.heading: Community decisions cannot be made by a few
outline.gist: Muslim minorities in the West do this poorly: big decisions about money, direction and priorities need broad input, and no imam or institution may steer the community without coordinating with others.

outline.heading: The Prophet held back his view: leaving Madinah for Uhud
outline.gist: He asked for advice and kept his own opinion to himself so as not to sway people; outvoted, he put on his armour and refused to reverse the decision, and after the loss he was told to keep consulting.

outline.heading: Do Muslim institutions even try?
outline.gist: He doubts institutions across the city and North America care about the views of their congregations or of neighbouring institutions.

outline.heading: Consultation is not for rulings
outline.gist: Legal rulings belong to those who spent years studying; consultation covers direction, resources and priorities.

outline.heading: Listening to needs: the community survey
outline.gist: The masjid's social innovation lab surveys people's needs, fears and struggles as a modern form of shura; what remains is institutions coordinating with each other.

outline.heading: Interlude
Sincerity is one to One, yet the surah is named for groups
outline.gist: Sincerity means pleasing no one but Allah in your heart, but it does not require living alone; the name az-Zumar points to groups.

outline.heading: No one walks to Jannah alone: choose your group
outline.gist: Believers and disbelievers are both driven in groups; find the people who will walk you to Paradise or a group of Hell will find you, since you rise with those you loved, meaning those you invested your time and care in.

outline.heading: Closed gates for Hell, open gates for Paradise
outline.gist: A host who opens the door before you arrive is hospitable; the people of Hell must knock at closed gates while the gates of Paradise open as its people approach. He tells of a friend who took seven minutes to answer his door.

outline.heading: Did no messengers come to you?
outline.gist: The keepers cannot understand how anyone who was warned could end up there; Allah did not make it hard to love or obey Him, so arriving there is shameful.

outline.heading: We heard but did not listen
outline.gist: The keepers assume some excuse, but the people admit they received the message and ignored it.

outline.heading: Interlude
The believer of Pharaoh's family
outline.gist: An example of dawah joined with connection to Allah: a man who concealed his faith for most of his life speaks up when they plan to kill Musa.

outline.heading: Concealing faith for a valid reason
outline.gist: Some people cannot practise openly for valid reasons, and Allah accepts from them.

outline.heading: Answering a thought with the sword is bankruptcy
outline.gist: Would you kill a man for saying my Lord is Allah? The verse is an argument for freedom of belief: meeting words with violence shows you have no better idea and no self-control.

outline.heading: Cancellation as persecution
outline.gist: Dictatorships make critics disappear; here people are cancelled, losing jobs and reputation, which he sees as no different, echoing the Arabic saying that cutting provision is like cutting off the head.

outline.heading: The shrinking range of acceptable opinion
outline.gist: Governments and other groups now limit what can be said in public; he has seen physicians sent through months of remediation for an overheard remark.

outline.heading: Since October 7: the condemnation trap
outline.gist: The constant demand that Muslims condemn was used to keep them from speaking about what was happening every day, and the space to speak against Zionism is still missing.

outline.heading: Zionism is an ideology, not Judaism
outline.gist: Muslims do not hate Jews, who are closest to them in faith, related by blood and have lived among Muslims for millennia; Zionism is a dangerous ideology that denies others the right to live in their ancestral lands.

outline.heading: Advocacy and organisation must change
outline.gist: For anything to change, the community's advocacy and organisation must grow so it has the pull to protect its people; he recalls being pressed to speak on the radio about a sensitive issue.

outline.heading: Clergy speak freely because institutions back them
outline.gist: Church clergy say far more aggressive things without being cancelled because their churches stand behind them, while an imam who misspeaks is left alone.

outline.heading: His teacher: stand up and I will answer
outline.gist: A teacher once refused an anonymous dangerous question unless the asker stood with him; people who demand public statements should share the risk or work communally to protect the speaker.

outline.heading: Brave with someone else's life
outline.gist: Demanding courage from imams while risking nothing is a toxic narrative; imams who challenge the status quo are routinely cut off, so support them first and push opinion out as a community effort.

outline.heading: If he lies, the lie is his burden
outline.gist: If the man is lying his lie will catch up with him, and if truthful you will be struck by what he warns of; this believer escaped alive, a rare happy ending, unlike the man in Ya-Sin.

outline.heading: Interlude
Good and evil are never equal: repel with the best
outline.gist: Answer the harm people do to you with the best you have, not merely with good; it is easy to say and borderline impossible to do.

outline.heading: Your enemy becomes a close friend
outline.gist: Most people who harm others are struggling or weak; met with excellence, nearly all calm down, reassess and seek friendship.

outline.heading: It takes grit and humility, and it works
outline.gist: It requires courage, sincerity and swallowing your ego; if you cannot articulate Islam, this is your dawah, and he testifies from experience that it works.

outline.heading: Interlude
His teacher's favourite verse: dawah in short commands
outline.gist: The verse is cut into small pieces, each one a way Muslims carry their dawah.

outline.heading: Call, stay upright, believe in every Book, be just
outline.gist: Keep calling and stay on the straight path, do not follow people's whims, believe in every revealed scripture, and treat others with justice and equality.

outline.heading: Our deeds and your deeds: Allah will judge
outline.gist: Each side lives by its conviction and argument may reach a dead end; the Muslim outlook combines identity and clarity with tolerance: I invite you, I will not persecute you, and Allah will judge between us.

outline.heading: Interlude
Arguing about Allah's signs without proof
outline.gist: Those who dispute Allah's signs and existence have no argument that can stand; the real cause lies in their chests.

outline.heading: Arrogance: acting from a status you do not have
outline.gist: Arrogance is believing yourself above where you are and treating people from there, such as looking down on religious people's flaws and rejecting their message; we are all equal.

outline.heading: Seek refuge from arrogance
outline.gist: Ask Allah's protection from ever looking down on others as ignorant, weak or unworthy of compassion; nothing worse can live in the heart.

themes.note: The Ha-Mim surahs as a manual: dawah to opponents with dua, through behaviour, with a reference and consultation.

themes.label: Freedom, rights and responsibility

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Since October 7 Muslims have been kept from speaking; Zionism is an ideology distinct from Judaism.

themes.label: Activism, civic engagement and the path forward

themes.note: Conviction and justice side by side: invite, do not persecute, and leave judgment to Allah.

themes.note: Arrogance underlies rejection of Allah's signs; seek refuge from looking down on anyone.

Push back against evil with the best you have

2:219.ar: ۞يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡخَمۡرِ وَٱلۡمَيۡسِرِۖ قُلۡ فِيهِمَآ إِثۡمࣱ كَبِيرࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثۡمُهُمَآ أَكۡبَرُ مِن نَّفۡعِهِمَاۗ وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَۖ قُلِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ
2:219.en: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, "In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you what they should spend. Say, "The excess [beyond needs]." Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses [of revelation] that you might give thought

4:149.ar: إِن تُبۡدُواْ خَيۡرًا أَوۡ تُخۡفُوهُ أَوۡ تَعۡفُواْ عَن سُوٓءࣲ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوࣰّ ا قَدِيرًا
4:149.en: If [instead] you show [some] good or conceal it or pardon an offense - indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent

25:70.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتࣲۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:70.en: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful

2:51.ar: وَإِذۡ وَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
2:51.en: And [recall] when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights. Then you took [for worship] the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers

2:52.ar: ثُمَّ عَفَوۡنَا عَنكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:52.en: Then We forgave you after that so perhaps you would be grateful

2:55.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهۡرَةࣰ فَأَخَذَتۡكُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:55.en: And [recall] when you said, "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah outright"; so the thunderbolt took you while you were looking on

2:56.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوۡتِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:56.en: Then We revived you after your death that perhaps you would be grateful

3:152.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥٓ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَۚ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمۡ عَنۡهُمۡ لِيَبۡتَلِيَكُمۡۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا عَنكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
3:152.en: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing the enemy by His permission until [the time] when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the order [given by the Prophet] and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then he turned you back from them [defeated] that He might test you. And He has already forgiven you, and Allah is the possessor of bounty for the believers

3:155.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوۡاْ مِنكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ إِنَّمَا ٱسۡتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بِبَعۡضِ مَا كَسَبُواْۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
3:155.en: Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some [blame] they had earned. But Allah has already forgiven them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing

4:43.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَنتُمۡ سُكَٰرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعۡلَمُواْ مَا تَقُولُونَ وَلَا جُنُبًا إِلَّا عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّىٰ تَغۡتَسِلُواْۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ أَحَدࣱ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡغَآئِطِ أَوۡ لَٰمَسۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَلَمۡ تَجِدُواْ مَآءࣰ فَتَيَمَّمُواْ صَعِيدࣰ ا طَيِّبࣰ ا فَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِوُجُوهِكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا
4:43.en: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying or in a state of janabah, except those passing through [a place of prayer], until you have washed [your whole body]. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and your hands [with it]. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving

58:2.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمۡۖ إِنۡ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّا ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي وَلَدۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَزُورࣰ اۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
58:2.en: Those who pronounce thihar among you [to separate] from their wives - they are not [consequently] their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they are saying an objectionable statement and a falsehood. But indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving

22:60.ar: ۞ذَٰلِكَۖ وَمَنۡ عَاقَبَ بِمِثۡلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِۦ ثُمَّ بُغِيَ عَلَيۡهِ لَيَنصُرَنَّهُ ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
22:60.en: That [is so]. And whoever responds [to injustice] with the equivalent of that with which he was harmed and then is tyrannized - Allah will surely aid him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving

42:30.ar: وَمَآ أَصَٰبَكُم مِّن مُّصِيبَةࣲ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِيكُمۡ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَن كَثِيرࣲ‏
42:30.en: And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned; but He pardons much

42:25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
42:25.en: And it is He who accepts repentance from his servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do

24:22.ar: وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلۡيَعۡفُواْ وَلۡيَصۡفَحُوٓاْۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
24:22.en: And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

3:134.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِي ٱلسَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَٱلۡكَٰظِمِينَ ٱلۡغَيۡظَ وَٱلۡعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
3:134.en: Who spend [in the cause of Allah] during ease and hardship and who restrain anger and who pardon the people - and Allah loves the doers of good

12:91.ar: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدۡ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
12:91.en: They said, "By Allah, certainly has Allah preferred you over us, and indeed, we have been sinners

12:92.ar: قَالَ لَا تَثۡرِيبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ يَغۡفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
12:92.en: He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful

Kttjn4j-quk.speaker: adnan
Kttjn4j-quk.speaker_note: Ramadan morning Names of Allah series in his voice, given before the 27th night
Kttjn4j-quk.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-'Afuw (The Pardoner)
Kttjn4j-quk.one_line: Al-'Afuw, who erases sin entirely and replaces it with reward, and how pardoning others and leaving the past behind lets us renew ourselves.
Kttjn4j-quk.summary: On the eve of the 27th night he takes Al-'Afuw from the names of self-renewal. The root means erasing traces and surplus, so pardon moves a person from a negative to a high positive: the sin is removed, its residue wiped, Allah is pleased and reward is given. Forgiveness covers a sin that still appears in the record; pardon removes it so completely that the angel who wrote it, the person harmed and eventually you yourself forget it. That is why the Prophet taught Aisha to ask for pardon on the Night of Power. The name pairs with the Able, since pardon means something only from a position of power, and the early Muslims' hope in it came from knowing Allah, not from belittling their sins. He shows the Quran attaching pardon to the gravest failures: the calf, demanding to see Allah, the retreat at Uhud, praying drunk, and the oppression of zihar. Two applications follow. Pardon others, which is harder than forgiving because it means never raising the matter again and restoring trust, as Abu Bakr did with Mistah and the Prophet did at the conquest of Makkah. And use Allah's pardon for self-renewal: after settling what you owe people, stop carrying past sins and compete again on level ground.

outline.heading: Opening
Meaning of 'afw: erasing traces, from negative to high positive
outline.gist: Wind erasing tracks and 'give what is surplus'; His pardon removes the sin and its residue, then brings His pleasure and reward.

outline.heading: Maghfirah: the covered sin
outline.gist: Forgiveness means the sin is still in your book but stamped as concealed and forgiven.

outline.heading: Pardon: the sin is gone from the book
outline.gist: An imagined search on Judgment Day: the page is empty, the recording angel and the wronged person do not remember, and Allah says He pardoned it.

outline.heading: Aisha's dua for the Night of Power
outline.gist: O Allah, You are the Pardoner and love to pardon, so pardon me; pardon is one degree above forgiveness.

outline.heading: Paired with the Concealer and the Able
outline.gist: He conceals then pardons, and pardon is meaningful only from someone with the power to take back their right.

outline.heading: The 27th night and pardon
outline.gist: The scholars he lived with always associated this night with seeking Allah's pardon.

outline.heading: If You ask me about my sins, I will ask about Your pardon
outline.gist: Early scholars' hope grew from knowing Allah's status, unlike deluded hope that comes from not seeing one's sins as serious.

outline.heading: Pardon written on the Prophet's sword
outline.gist: Pardon whoever wronged you: the sword that restored rights was carried with the principle of pardoning once able.

outline.heading: Sins turned into good deeds
outline.gist: Pardon flips a sin into a good deed, a gift for those ashamed of their sins.

outline.heading: Pardon after the golden calf
outline.gist: Days after seeing the sea split, the Israelites worshipped a calf, and still Allah pardoned them.

outline.heading: Pardon after demanding to see Allah
outline.gist: They were struck dead, revived and pardoned.

outline.heading: Pardon twice at Uhud
outline.gist: Archers who left the mountain for the spoils and those who fled were pardoned.

outline.heading: Pardon in praying drunk and in zihar
outline.gist: Verses on prayer while intoxicated and on men oppressing wives by zihar end with Allah as Pardoner.

outline.heading: The oppressed who retaliates; calamities and much pardoned
outline.gist: Even one who goes too far in retaliating is pardoned; hardships expiate mistakes and Allah pardons much.

outline.heading: Entering Paradise without reckoning
outline.gist: He accepts repentance and pardons; seventy thousand and more enter with no account, like a legal pardon that wipes a record.

outline.heading: Big sins need pardon so they stop haunting you
outline.gist: Learn from sin and repent, but know it can be removed and even flipped; that is what this night offers.

outline.heading: Living the name 1: pardon others, as Abu Bakr did Mistah
outline.gist: Abu Bakr vowed to stop supporting the relative who spread the slander about Aisha, until the verse asked, do you not love that Allah forgive you.

outline.heading: Pardon is harder than forgiveness
outline.gist: Forgiveness reaches neutral; pardon never raises the matter again and restores the relationship, perhaps better than before.

outline.heading: The servant girl and the hot water
outline.gist: A servant's accident killed a man's child; she recited the verse on restraining anger and pardoning, and he freed her.

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan with no way back
outline.gist: After years of enmity and lying to the Prophet about the broken treaty, he was told to use the words of Yusuf's brothers, knowing the Prophet loved to follow earlier prophets.

outline.heading: No blame on you today
outline.gist: The Prophet answered with Yusuf's words, leaving no hard feelings; Abu Sufyan marvelled at his forbearance.

outline.heading: Go, you are free: the people of Makkah released
outline.gist: Those who had fought him for years were gathered and pardoned for the sake of Allah.

outline.heading: Just let it go
outline.gist: Holding a grudge only weighs on you; Allah will never let a servant outdo Him in pardoning.

outline.heading: Living the name 2: self-renewal
outline.gist: After settling what you owe people, let Allah's pardon lift the weight of past sins so you can stand straight, regain ambition and compete on level ground.

42:47.ar: ٱسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِرَبِّكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ يَوۡمࣱ لَّا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ مَا لَكُم مِّن مَّلۡجَإࣲ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّكِيرࣲ‏
42:47.en: Respond to your Lord before a Day comes from Allah of which there is no repelling. No refuge will you have that day, nor for you will there be any denial

42:52.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ رُوحࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَمۡرِنَاۚ مَا كُنتَ تَدۡرِي مَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ وَلَا ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ وَلَٰكِن جَعَلۡنَٰهُ نُورࣰ ا نَّهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِنَاۚ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهۡدِيٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
42:52.en: And thus We have revealed to you an inspiration of Our command. You did not know what is the Book or [what is] faith, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, [O Muhammad], you guide to a straight path

42:53.ar: صِرَٰطِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ أَلَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَصِيرُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
42:53.en: The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah do [all] matters evolve

43:51.ar: وَنَادَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فِي قَوۡمِهِۦ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَيۡسَ لِي مُلۡكُ مِصۡرَ وَهَٰذِهِ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
43:51.en: And Pharaoh called out among his people; he said, "O my people, does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me; then do you not see

43:52.ar: أَمۡ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينࣱ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
43:52.en: Or am I [not] better than this one who is insignificant and hardly makes himself clear

43:53.ar: فَلَوۡلَآ أُلۡقِيَ عَلَيۡهِ أَسۡوِرَةࣱ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ مُقۡتَرِنِينَ
43:53.en: Then why have there not been placed upon him bracelets of gold or come with him the angels in conjunction

43:54.ar: فَٱسۡتَخَفَّ قَوۡمَهُۥ فَأَطَاعُوهُۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
43:54.en: So he bluffed his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were [themselves] a people defiantly disobedient [of Allah]

43:67.ar: ٱلۡأَخِلَّآءُ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بَعۡضُهُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
43:67.en: Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to each other, except for the righteous

44:38.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ
44:38.en: And We did not create the heavens and earth and that between them in play

44:39.ar: مَا خَلَقۡنَٰهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
44:39.en: We did not create them except in truth, but most of them do not know

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded

46:15.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۖ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرۡهࣰ ا وَوَضَعَتۡهُ كُرۡهࣰ اۖ وَحَمۡلُهُۥ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ ثَلَٰثُونَ شَهۡرًاۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَبَلَغَ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰ قَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا تَرۡضَىٰهُ وَأَصۡلِحۡ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِيٓۖ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
46:15.en: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning [period] is thirty months. [He grows] until, when he reaches maturity and reaches [the age of] forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to work righteousness of which You will approve and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims

46:16.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنۡهُمۡ أَحۡسَنَ مَا عَمِلُواْ وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَن سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ وَعۡدَ ٱلصِّدۡقِ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ
46:16.en: Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds, [their being] among the companions of Paradise. [That is] the promise of truth which they had been promised

46:17.ar: وَٱلَّذِي قَالَ لِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ أُفࣲّ لَّكُمَآ أَتَعِدَانِنِيٓ أَنۡ أُخۡرَجَ وَقَدۡ خَلَتِ ٱلۡقُرُونُ مِن قَبۡلِي وَهُمَا يَسۡتَغِيثَانِ ٱللَّهَ وَيۡلَكَ ءَامِنۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ فَيَقُولُ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
46:17.en: But one who says to his parents, "Uff to you; do you promise me that I will be brought forth [from the earth] when generations before me have already passed on [into oblivion]?" while they call to Allah for help [and to their son], "Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth." But he says, "This is not but legends of the former people

46:18.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ فِيٓ أُمَمࣲ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
46:18.en: Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect, [who will be] among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they [all] were losers

46:19.ar: وَلِكُلࣲّ دَرَجَٰتࣱ مِّمَّا عَمِلُواْۖ وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
46:19.en: And for all there are degrees [of reward and punishment] for what they have done, and [it is] so that He may fully compensate them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged

46:21.ar: ۞وَٱذۡكُرۡ أَخَا عَادٍ إِذۡ أَنذَرَ قَوۡمَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَحۡقَافِ وَقَدۡ خَلَتِ ٱلنُّذُرُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦٓ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
46:21.en: And mention, [O Muhammad], the brother of 'Aad, when he warned his people in the [region of] al-Ahqaf - and warners had already passed on before him and after him - [saying], "Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day

46:29.ar: وَإِذۡ صَرَفۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ نَفَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالُوٓاْ أَنصِتُواْۖ فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوۡاْ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِم مُّنذِرِينَ
46:29.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We directed to you a few of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, "Listen quietly." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners

2:186.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِۖ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلۡيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِي لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡشُدُونَ
2:186.en: And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided

28:34.ar: وَأَخِي هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفۡصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانࣰ ا فَأَرۡسِلۡهُ مَعِيَ رِدۡءࣰ ا يُصَدِّقُنِيٓۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
28:34.en: And my brother Aaron is more fluent than me in tongue, so send him with me as support, verifying me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me

25:43.ar: أَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِ وَكِيلًا
25:43.en: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him

_c37Q1hcvB8.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 24: Quranic Reflections (Ash-Shura 24 to the end of Al-Ahqaf)
_c37Q1hcvB8.one_line: The Ha-Mim warnings for those carrying dawah: materialism, delusion, arrogance in knowledge, and accepting that outcomes belong to Allah; plus friendship, mockery and responding to Allah now.
_c37Q1hcvB8.summary: He finishes the Ha-Mim cluster on carrying Islam to individuals. After recalling the three positive pieces of advice from Ghafir, Fussilat and Ash-Shura, he presents the three warnings: az-Zukhruf against judging by glitter and running religious life like a business, ad-Dukhan against delusional optimism that ignores the signs, and al-Jathiyah against arrogance born of knowledge. Al-Ahqaf closes by reminding that even perfect effort does not control who responds, as Hud's people refused while jinn listened unbidden. From Ash-Shura he urges responding to Allah now, as fully as you can rather than perfectly, while you can still repent, and describes the Quran as a spirit that gives life and a light that guides. Az-Zukhruf's verse on close friends becoming enemies leads to a long reflection on love for Allah's sake, which must be proven by helping each other toward Him, and on choosing companions as the most important decision of life. Pharaoh's mockery of Musa's speech shows the hollow logic of materialism and the danger of ridiculing what people cannot control. Ad-Dukhan reminds that creation is serious, and al-Jathiyah warns that a knowledgeable person can still make his desires his god. He ends by lifting the burden of judging where others will end up.

outline.heading: Opening
The Ha-Mim cluster: advice and warnings for dawah
outline.gist: Unlike the earlier cluster on establishing Islam as a civilisation, these seven surahs are operational advice on bringing individuals to Islam or to appreciating what they have.

outline.heading: Ghafir: take it to those who argue, while connected to Allah
outline.gist: Do not wait for people who ask; engage those who oppose, in parallel with your own dua.

outline.heading: Fussilat: dawah is best done through behaviour
outline.gist: Pushing words on people who refuse puts them in jeopardy, while achievements, character and ethics affect people more.

outline.heading: Ash-Shura: reference points and consultation
outline.gist: Have clear values to refer to and move as a community that has agreed on its direction.

outline.heading: Az-Zukhruf: the pitfall of materialism
outline.gist: Judging by what looks flashy rather than by substance, and running masjids and communities like businesses, will fail on the path of dawah.

outline.heading: Ad-Dukhan: delusional thinking and ignoring the signs
outline.gist: Telling yourself comforting lies and ignoring visible gaps dooms a community; this is why he keeps pointing out problems instead of indulging in blind optimism.

outline.heading: Al-Jathiyah: arrogance with knowledge
outline.gist: The Quran's profound values give Muslims insight, but if that knowledge leads to looking down on those without it or who refuse it, the decline is hard to recover from.

outline.heading: Al-Ahqaf: the outcome is in Allah's hands
outline.gist: Even if you follow every recommendation and avoid every warning, you cannot control who listens; sometimes the best job gets no response.

outline.heading: Hud's people refused; the jinn listened unbidden
outline.gist: Hud did everything right and was rejected, while jinn the Prophet never addressed heard and believed; the same uncertainty applies to raising your children.

outline.heading: Not bulletproof, but required
outline.gist: The surah ends the cluster to say the advice does not always work, yet it must be followed; dua keeps dawah from becoming I am right and you are wrong instead of wanting to share a blessing.

outline.heading: Musa did everything right
outline.gist: Each of these surahs carries Musa's story because he followed every recommendation and avoided every pitfall, and still did not get the response he hoped for.

outline.heading: Interlude
Respond to your Lord before the day with no return
outline.gist: Respond to His teachings, commands and recommendations now; once you stand before Him there is no going back to try again.

outline.heading: No refuge and no slap on the wrist
outline.gist: There is nowhere to hide that day and no lenient reproach; the judgment is final with no appeal, which sums up the whole surah.

outline.heading: Respond, not obey flawlessly
outline.gist: Allah asks us to respond, not to be perfect, because He acknowledges our deficits; as He answers our dua, we answer Him by prioritising His commands and trying our best.

outline.heading: Watch your own response, not others'
outline.gist: Each person's capacity differs, so spend less time judging how others follow and more on whether your own response is your best.

outline.heading: The priceless chance to fix things now
outline.gist: Right now you can repent and change immediately; that opportunity is priceless because it will soon be gone.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Quran as a spirit and a light
outline.gist: Allah describes the revelation as a spirit from His command, something alive that gives life, revealed to a Prophet who knew nothing of scripture.

outline.heading: Guiding to the straight path by the light you carry
outline.gist: People were dead inside and the Quran revived them; because the Prophet carries that beacon he guides to the path of Allah, to whom all matters return.

outline.heading: Close friends become enemies, except the God-conscious
outline.gist: On Judgment Day the closest friends will want nothing to do with each other unless they shared mindfulness of Allah.

outline.heading: Friends remind you of what you did together
outline.gist: That day you will see each friendship only by which side of the scale your time together falls on; time not spent helping each other toward Allah turns love into contempt.

outline.heading: Those who love for Allah on pulpits of light
outline.gist: Those who love one another for Allah's sake will stand on pulpits of light so honoured that prophets admire them.

outline.heading: What love for Allah's sake means
outline.gist: A friendship with no worldly calculation, built on each helping the other become closer to Allah and a better person.

outline.heading: Love needs proof
outline.gist: Love in Islam is not just a feeling; without encouraging each other to good and away from bad it is meaningless, while real love offers hope.

outline.heading: Hold on to friends who draw you closer
outline.gist: Such people are rare; an intimate relationship ends either as something envied or as enmity.

outline.heading: Choose your company more carefully than your car
outline.gist: Be picky about friends, the most important decision of your life; people spend months choosing a car but little thought on who surrounds them, which decides their Judgment Day.

outline.heading: Interlude
Pharaoh's case against Musa, told only here
outline.gist: Friendships built on material benefit fail, and az-Zukhruf alone records Pharaoh arguing why his people should follow him and not Musa.

outline.heading: Am I not better? Mocking Musa's speech
outline.gist: Pharaoh boasts of Egypt's rivers and sovereignty and belittles Musa as unprotected and unable to speak clearly; Musa knew his weakness and asked for Harun as a more eloquent partner.

outline.heading: The logic of materialism
outline.gist: Musa is beloved and revered, yet Pharaoh judges by strength, wealth and fluency and asks why he has no gold bracelets or escorting angels; none of it bears on the message.

outline.heading: He made fools of his people
outline.gist: Pharaoh treated his people as fools and they obeyed; the argument was hollow and offensive.

outline.heading: Beware of mocking what people cannot control
outline.gist: Mockery and satire are dangerous even among friends; ridiculing a trait someone did not choose is below the belt, and if people do it to you, do not sink to their level.

outline.heading: Attacking the person when you cannot beat the idea
outline.gist: Losing debaters dig up a bad photo or a past flaw to shift attention; Pharaoh, ruler of Egypt, feared Musa because a strong idea frightens power.

outline.heading: Interlude
Not created in play, but with truth
outline.gist: Within ad-Dukhan's warning against delusion, Allah says He did not create the heavens and earth in jest but with truth; existence is serious.

outline.heading: The Prophet joked, but never about serious things
outline.gist: Things prevail only through truth and crumble against it; take yourself lightly if you like, as the Prophet smiled and joked often, but know where the line is.

outline.heading: A book filled with play
outline.gist: Hold yourself to the standard of truth you will be judged by; a record of endless play with no commitment, grit or serious decisions will not end well.

outline.heading: Taking desire as one's god
outline.gist: Al-Jathiyah warns against arrogance with knowledge: have you seen the one who takes his whims as the one he worships?

outline.heading: Your god is whatever you obey without question
outline.gist: No religion literally worships desire, so this figure of speech shows how Allah defines worship: what you obey immediately and never question.

outline.heading: Actions prove whom you worship
outline.gist: When the scales of reason weigh a dilemma and the self always wins, desire is your god whatever you claim.

outline.heading: Misguided despite knowledge
outline.gist: Unlike the similar verse in al-Furqan, this one adds that he was led astray knowingly; knowledge that does not help you control urges and tell revelation from the self's selfishness has no value.

outline.heading: Knowledge without guidance, and the sealed heart
outline.gist: Such knowledge only breeds arrogance, vanity and envy, and increases distance from Allah; hearing, heart and sight are sealed.

outline.heading: Admit you are far and keep fighting
outline.gist: Acknowledging you are not doing well need not make you despair, but without it there is no fight against the self; even if you are losing, put up the fight.

outline.heading: Using knowledge to serve the self
outline.gist: Once you defend whatever you want as right, you use knowledgeable arguments to serve hidden struggles for power and position while sealed off from insight.

outline.heading: Interlude
The dutiful child and the defiant one
outline.gist: Al-Ahqaf contrasts the person kind to his parents and children who loves Allah, whose good is accepted and bad forgiven, with the one who rebukes his parents and rejects Allah.

outline.heading: Degrees for everyone, and no one wronged
outline.gist: Each group receives ranks according to what it did and no one is treated unjustly; you control neither who believes nor who is rewarded.

outline.heading: A burden lifted
outline.gist: Where others end up is not your business; follow the recommendations, heed the warnings and leave the rest to Allah.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: The Ha-Mim surahs as three recommendations and three warnings for carrying Islam to individuals.

themes.label: Modernity, secularism, materialism and their effects
themes.note: Materialistic judgment by appearance and treating religious work like business.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Delusional optimism that ignores the community's real gaps.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Do everything right and still leave results to Allah, as Hud and Musa did.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Respond to Allah as fully as you can, not flawlessly, and attend to your own response.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: The present chance to repent and change is priceless because it ends.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran as a life-giving spirit and a guiding light.

themes.label: Brotherhood, companionship and friendship
themes.note: Friendships turn to enmity unless built on helping each other toward Allah; choosing company is life's most important decision.

themes.label: Guarding the tongue; speech and gossip
themes.note: Mocking traits people cannot control, and attacking the person instead of the idea.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Creation is serious and made with truth; a life of endless play fails that standard.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Knowledge without guidance breeds arrogance and lets desire become one's god.

themes.label: Withholding judgment of others
themes.note: Where people end up is Allah's business, not ours.

35:41.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمۡسِكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ أَن تَزُولَاۚ وَلَئِن زَالَتَآ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَهُمَا مِنۡ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورࣰ ا
35:41.en: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving

36:38.ar: وَٱلشَّمۡسُ تَجۡرِي لِمُسۡتَقَرࣲّ لَّهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
36:38.en: And the sun runs [on course] toward its stopping point. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allah] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allah] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

48:7.ar: وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا
48:7.en: And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise

8:11.ar: إِذۡ يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةࣰ مِّنۡهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ لِّيُطَهِّرَكُم بِهِۦ وَيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمۡ رِجۡزَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ وَلِيَرۡبِطَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُمۡ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ ٱلۡأَقۡدَامَ
8:11.en: [Remember] when He overwhelmed you with drowsiness [giving] security from Him and sent down upon you from the sky, rain by which to purify you and remove from you the evil [suggestions] of Satan and to make steadfast your hearts and plant firmly thereby your feet

8:43.ar: إِذۡ يُرِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلࣰ اۖ وَلَوۡ أَرَىٰكَهُمۡ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّفَشِلۡتُمۡ وَلَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَلَّمَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
8:43.en: [Remember, O Muhammad], when Allah showed them to you in your dream as few; and if He had shown them to you as many, you [believers] would have lost courage and would have disputed in the matter [of whether to fight], but Allah saved [you from that]. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts

8:44.ar: وَإِذۡ يُرِيكُمُوهُمۡ إِذِ ٱلۡتَقَيۡتُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِكُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا وَيُقَلِّلُكُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِهِمۡ لِيَقۡضِيَ ٱللَّهُ أَمۡرࣰ ا كَانَ مَفۡعُولࣰ اۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
8:44.en: And [remember] when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and He made you [appear] as few in their eyes so that Allah might accomplish a matter already destined. And to Allah are [all] matters returned

8:10.ar: وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشۡرَىٰ وَلِتَطۡمَئِنَّ بِهِۦ قُلُوبُكُمۡۚ وَمَا ٱلنَّصۡرُ إِلَّا مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
8:10.en: And Allah made it not but good tidings and so that your hearts would be assured thereby. And victory is not but from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

33:25.ar: وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِغَيۡظِهِمۡ لَمۡ يَنَالُواْ خَيۡرࣰ اۚ وَكَفَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱلۡقِتَالَۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ قَوِيًّا عَزِيزࣰ ا
33:25.en: And Allah repelled those who disbelieved, in their rage, not having obtained any good. And sufficient was Allah for the believers in battle, and ever is Allah Powerful and Exalted in Might

30:5.ar: بِنَصۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ يَنصُرُ مَن يَشَآءُۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
30:5.en: In the victory of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful

27:9.ar: يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
27:9.en: O Moses, indeed it is I - Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise

4:158.ar: بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡهِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:158.en: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise

9:40.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودࣲ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفۡلَىٰۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلۡعُلۡيَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
9:40.en: If you do not aid the Prophet - Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved had driven him out [of Makkah] as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." And Allah sent down his tranquillity upon him and supported him with angels you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah - that is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

5:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِيٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِحَقٍّۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِي وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِكَۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
5:116.en: And [beware the Day] when Allah will say, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You!
